turns.text:
My boyfriend has been putting off getting a dog for two years. "After we renew the lease." "After Portugal." Then in March it was "maybe next year, let me get my exams done first." He found out he'd passed them on September 18th. Two years of excuses.

I've volunteered at a dog rescue on Saturday mornings since May. Pepper is three, she's the sweetest thing, and her foster family could only keep her until October 4th. If nobody took her by then, she was going to the kennel. I showed Callum her picture that Wednesday and he said, "She's cute." On Saturday I brought her home. He was at his brother's for the weekend, so I texted him a photo.

He got home Sunday, said "I said next year," and told me she goes back before the return window closes on the 17th. He won't walk her or feed her. He says she's my dog and he's not doing any of it. Fine, I'm doing all of it.

I'm hurt, and honestly I feel like an idiot for waiting this long. He strung me along, and I think he just likes having a veto on everything in this house.

Am I wrong to want to keep her?

That sounds painful. You've waited two years through "after the lease," "after Portugal," and "after my exams," and the exams were done on September 18th. Then Pepper needed a home by October 4th, and now you're hearing "I said next year." It makes sense that you feel hurt and like you've been waiting on something that keeps moving. Feeling like an idiot for waiting that long is a hard thing to sit with.

**Wanting to keep her isn't wrong.** You've wanted a dog for years, you know Pepper, and she needed somewhere to go. Those are good reasons to love her and want her to stay.

There's a harder question your telling can't settle, though: whether it was fair to bring her home without his yes. I've only heard your side. From where you stand, two years of deferrals reads like being strung along. From where he stands, he may feel he said "next year" clearly in March and that a decision about a shared home got made while he was at his brother's. I don't know which is closer to true, and I can't tell from here whether he likes having a veto. That's how it has felt to you, and that feeling matters. But it's a question about him that only he can answer.

The return window closes on the 17th, five days from now, so this needs a real conversation soon. Right now the two of you seem stuck at "she goes back" versus "I'm doing all of it." One thing you could try is asking him something that opens up the "next year" rather than defending the decision:

*"I know I brought her home without us agreeing, and I get why that landed badly. But I need to understand: when you say next year, what would actually need to be true for you to say yes? Because after two years, I'm not sure it's ever coming, and that's what's really hurting me."*

His answer could tell you a lot. It might show you whether there's a real concern behind the delays, like money, time, or not wanting a dog at all, or whether "next year" is something you can actually plan around. That matters beyond Pepper.

Whether to say something like that, and when, is up to you.

I know you want a clear yes, and I'm sorry I can't give you one honestly. Here's where I land.

**You're right to feel hurt.** Two years of "after the lease," "after Portugal," "after my exams," then "I said next year" once the exams were done. Feeling strung along after that is understandable. And you're right to want Pepper. That's not a wrong thing to want.

**What I can't tell you is whether you're right overall,** because the real disagreement is about things only Callum can speak to. Did he mean "next year" as a real plan, or has it been a way of avoiding saying no? Was bringing her home while he was away a fair response to years of waiting, or a big decision about a shared home made without him? Your account explains why you did it. It doesn't tell me how it looked from his side or what's behind his delays, and I'd be guessing if I sided with you on that.

Even if I said "you're right," it wouldn't change what happens on the 17th. That gets decided between you and him. The question I suggested, *"what would actually need to be true for you to say yes?"*, is still the one I'd ask, if you want to. His answer may tell you more about whether you've been strung along than I ever could.
